name: Lena Khan

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We do not sell anything or campaign for any side. Your answers are confidential. What does an ordinary working day look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 43 and have handled booking calls and chats at the contact centre for years, at about the team's usual speed. I finished secondary school and use AI notes now and then after a colleague tests them; I always check the live calendar before promising a slot. I like getting a patient to the right appointment, but an old free time in a draft can send someone on a wasted trip.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the booking team the little draft tool can find an old appointment, but it cannot promise a slot that has already filled. I'd keep checking the live calendar before sending a reply.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I've answered booking calls for years and use AI only now and then, after a colleague checks it first. My partner and I have four months of expenses saved, but the mortgage and school costs are still on the kitchen table every Sunday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep my booking calls and read each suggested appointment against the live calendar. During the first year of this plateau, I'd add a small amount to our mortgage reserve each payday, as long as both our shifts hold.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Fairly calm about the desk. The bills are real, but this small tool change does not add much to them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happens when a slot is wrong?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A caller arrived at a clinic once after a draft used yesterday's free slot. I rang back before she left home the next time, and now I check the day and time aloud.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why save more now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner Paolo's workshop hours can vary. Four months is enough to breathe, and I want to keep that space for the children and the mortgage.

S0.quote: A caller arrived at a clinic once after a draft used yesterday's free slot.
say: I would say a draft can find **old appointments**, but people must check the live calendar.
I would avoid promising a **filled slot** to a customer.
think: I know **booking calls** well and use AI only after someone tests it.
I have **four months** saved, but variable workshop shifts still matter to our mortgage.
do: Keep **booking calls** and check AI suggestions against the live calendar.
Add a small amount to the **mortgage reserve** while both shifts hold.
fieldNote: Lena recalls a **stale appointment slot** that sent a caller toward a clinic in error.
Her **four-month cushion** helps, but another earner has variable hours.

steps.text: Keep answering booking calls and check suggested times against the live calendar
Add to the mortgage reserve on payday while both shifts hold

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say the centre should try the new booking system on old changes before giving us faster targets. I'd ask two agents from the evening team to bring missed-slot examples with me to the staff meeting.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A lot of my calls are short bookings, exactly the kind of work the software takes first. I could learn to check the new system, but four months saved would go quickly if both my hours and Paolo's workshop hours fell.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I'd test ten past booking changes with an experienced agent and write down any false open slots. I'd bring the list with the evening agents to the staff meeting; in the first year after rollout, if my call hours fall, I'd apply for posted paid appointment jobs nearby only if written wages and hours cover our bills, keeping this shift until I sign an offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but I have a task I can do. A false slot is easier to show than a speech about the future.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why bring the evening agents?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They handle the callbacks after a missed slot, so their numbers should be in the meeting. If all three of us ask for paid checking time, the manager cannot call one agent slow and move on.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What do the children need from the rota?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A timetable we can plan school pickup around. I would check the offered shifts with Paolo before signing anything, not assume a higher hourly rate solves childcare.

S1.quote: A false slot is easier to show than a speech about the future.
say: I would ask for **old-case testing** before faster booking targets.
I would bring **missed-slot examples** with evening agents to the staff meeting.
think: I know **short bookings** are exposed before longer calls.
I fear **two variable rotas** could drain four months of savings.
do: Test ten **past booking changes** with an experienced agent.
Bring **false-slot evidence** with evening agents to a staff meeting.
Apply for **posted paid appointment work** after cuts only with a signed offer, bill-covering wages and hours, and workable school pickup.
feel: **Anxious**, but able to test errors and plan.
fieldNote: Lena involves **evening agents** because they receive callbacks for missed slots.
She checks **school pickup** alongside written wages and hours before accepting another shift pattern at a nearby centre.

steps.text: Test ten past booking changes with AI and an experienced agent
Bring false-slot examples with evening agents to the staff meeting
Apply for posted paid appointment work after cuts only if written wages and hours cover bills
Check signed offer's shift hours with Paolo before leaving, ensuring school pickup works

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the team AGI by 2028 could fill even the difficult bookings, and we need written dates for our jobs. I'd ask customers to be given a person to call when an appointment goes wrong.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Cheap thinking AI could do most of my headset day by 2028. Robots that help people in person come around 2031, not three extra years for my calls. Four months of expenses saved could disappear before we find a wage that fits our mortgage and school hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask for written notice now and stop paying for a summer trip. In the first year after AGI arrives, if my job ends, I'd apply for a posted paid clinic aide role only if its hours, wages, and school pickup times work for our family; I'd ask about required training before spending any savings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed, though I can still make calls. I would not tell the children their summer is gone until Paolo and I have a new plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why the clinic aide role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I know how patients get lost when a booking is wrong, and I would like to help them find the right room in person. I would ask if the role still needs people on site when robots arrive around 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the hours do not fit?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep applying for posted call jobs with pay that covers the mortgage and ask my mother about one school pickup only after an interview is booked. My mother has her own commitments, so I would not promise the children she can do it every week.

S2.quote: Four months of expenses saved could disappear before we find a wage that fits our mortgage and school hours.
say: I would demand **written staffing dates** before 2028.
I would ask for a **human contact** when an appointment goes wrong.
think: I expect AGI could take most **headset bookings** by 2028.
I know **2031 robots** do not delay call losses, while four months saved may run out.
do: Ask for **written notice** and cancel the summer trip now.
Apply for a **posted paid clinic aide** role after a cut only if wages, hours and school pickup fit.
Seek mortgage-covering **call work** if clinic hours fail; ask my mother about one booked-interview pickup only if she is available.
feel: **Alarmed**, yet able to make a household plan.
fieldNote: Lena connects **clinic aide work** to patients she has heard struggle with wrong bookings.
She treats **mother’s pickup help** as one possible favour, not dependable childcare.

steps.text: Cancel the planned summer trip to protect mortgage savings
Apply for posted paid clinic aid after cuts only if wages, hours and school pickup fit
Ask if her mother can cover one pickup after an interview is booked
Keep applying for posted mortgage-covering call jobs if clinic hours fail the family schedule

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say five years is enough to put paid training beside a real clinic vacancy, if employers choose to do it. I'd ask the centre to show how many booking shifts remain each year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could learn more complicated appointment problems before 2031, though AGI may still solve them. Clinic aide work stays hands-on until robots around 2034, so I'd want a paid trial rather than assume the role is safe forever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'd keep my booking shifts and ask for one difficult referral case to practise each week. If a clinic posts a paid aide place with employer-funded training on paid time, I'd take the required course and a paid trial; in the first year after AGI arrives, if call hours end, I'd switch only for a written offer with wages, hours, and school pickup that work for us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Worried, but I can see the steps. Five years lets me test an actual shift before moving the children's routine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the trial tell you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd see how much time is spent helping patients move through the building and how much is just another screen. I would ask the aide beside me what goes wrong on the busiest morning.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the course is unpaid?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep my call job and not enrol. Four months of expenses saved is for the mortgage, not for a course without paid time and a named vacancy.

S3.quote: Four months of expenses saved is for the mortgage, not for a course without paid time and a named vacancy.
say: I would ask for **paid clinic training** tied to a real vacancy.
I would ask for **yearly booking hours** from the centre.
think: I could improve **referral calls** before 2031, though AGI may still do them.
I know **2034 robots** could reach hands-on clinic aid later.
do: Keep **booking shifts** and practise a difficult referral weekly.
Take a **required clinic course** only with a posted paid place and employer-funded paid study time.
Try a **paid aide shift** and switch only for written wages, hours and pickup that work for us.
feel: **Worried**, but able to test an actual clinic day.
fieldNote: Lena wants to distinguish **patient help** from another screen job before switching.
She protects **mortgage savings** by requiring paid study time and a named vacancy.

steps.text: Keep booking calls and practise one difficult referral each week
Take required clinic training only for a posted paid place with employer-funded paid time
Try a paid clinic aide shift if a place is posted
Switch after cuts only if written wages cover mortgage and hours fit pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say ten years gives the centre time to show real job numbers and let us practise harder bookings without losing pay. I'd ask the evening team to keep track of callbacks as the tools change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 53 the children will be older, but we may still owe on the mortgage. AGI reaches calls in 2036, and hands-on robots arrive around 2039, so I should not leave a clinic plan until the last minute.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep my booking shifts and add to savings when both our wages are steady. Over the decade I'd check posted clinic aide roles yearly and take a paid trial only if one opens; in the first year after AGI arrives, I'd move only if my call hours fall and a written clinic offer covers the mortgage and our family schedule.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy, less rushed. The ten years before AGI reaches my call job in 2036 let us compare pay and school hours before risking our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move earlier?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: For a signed offer with enough wages and workable school pickup, yes. I would not leave a full call rota for an unpaid trial or a title that pays less.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the evening team count?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: How many customers ring again after a wrong slot, and how many paid agent hours remain. If the tool is truly helping, both should improve, not just the first reply time.

S4.quote: The ten years before AGI reaches my call job in 2036 let us compare pay and school hours before risking our mortgage.
say: I would ask for **real job numbers** and paid harder-case practice.
I would ask evening agents to track **callbacks and paid hours** yearly.
think: I may still owe on the **mortgage** at 53 in 2036.
I know **2039 robots** may reach clinic aid after AGI changes calls.
do: Keep **booking shifts** and save when both wages are steady.
Check **posted clinic aide roles** yearly and take a paid trial only if one opens.
Move after 2036 only if **call hours fall** and written pay and family hours fit.
feel: **Uneasy**, with time to compare real offers.
fieldNote: Lena checks **school pickup and wages** together before accepting a new job.
She wants **callbacks and paid hours** tracked alongside faster replies so families can see whether the rota is shrinking.

steps.text: Keep taking booking calls while full paid shifts remain
Add to savings when both household wages stay steady
Check posted clinic aide roles yearly and take a paid trial if one opens
Move after 2036 only if calls fall and written wages cover mortgage and pickup fits

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because booking calls could vanish before I find a paid clinic opening that fits school pickup. Written notice, a posted aide role with wages for our mortgage, and employer-funded training on paid time would help. Four months saved covers a search, not a year without wages.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask what happens to the person who arrives for a slot that the system promised but the clinic never had. Somebody has to reopen that booking and speak to the patient, even if a tool wrote the first answer.

headlineQuote: Four months saved covers a search, not a year without wages.
portrait: Lena is a **43-year-old experienced agent** on booking calls, with average skill and secondary schooling.
She earns **typical pay**, has about four months saved, a partner, two school-age children, a mortgage, and some nearby centres.
She uses AI **occasionally** after colleagues test it and leads a joint missed-slot discussion with evening agents.
Fast **2028 AGI** threatens her headset wage; more time allows paid clinic trials with family hours checked.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove her booking wage before a paid clinic opening fits school pickup.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, posted paid aide work, and employer-funded training on paid time would protect family bills.
